description: Lead filtering UI (#1083). The leads API tracks source, assigned_to, lifecycle_stage, tags, and score but the UI exposes no filters for them. Add filter controls to the leads client and make the leads API honor them. This is the one net-new feature in the bucket and is independent of the other features (could be parallelized).
steps: Read app/api/tenant/leads/route.ts to see how the GET list query is built and which query params it currently parses (search, pagination, etc.). Read components/tenant/leads-client-new.tsx (and leads-client.tsx if it is the active one — confirm which client the leads page renders) to see the existing filter/search UI pattern.

Extend the leads GET route to accept and apply filters: source, assignedTo (assigned_to), lifecycleStage (lifecycle_stage), tags (array/contains), and score range (scoreMin/scoreMax). Use Drizzle where-clause composition consistent with the existing query, and keep tenant scoping intact. Validate params with the existing zod pattern (lib/api/schemas.ts) rather than trusting raw input.

Add UI filter controls in the leads client following the existing filter component patterns (Select/dropdown for source, assigned_to, lifecycle_stage; tag multiselect or chips; numeric min/max inputs for score). Wire them into the existing fetch call as query params. Preserve current search + pagination behavior.

Populate filter option lists from real data where the pattern already exists (e.g. distinct sources, team members for assigned_to). If an options source is not readily available, use the known enum/lifecycle values and note it in findings.
Ensure filters combine with search and reset correctly (clearing a filter refetches).
acceptance_criteria: The leads GET API applies source, assigned_to, lifecycle_stage, tags, and score-range filters when the corresponding query params are provided, scoped to the tenant.
The leads page renders working filter controls for source, assigned_to, lifecycle_stage, tags, and score range.
Applying/clearing a filter refetches the list; existing search and pagination still work.
npm run typecheck and npm run lint pass with no new errors.
If there are unit tests for the leads route, they still pass; add/extend a unit test covering at least one new filter param if the test harness for that route already exists.
findings: Live client: app/tenant/leads/page.tsx renders components/tenant/leads-client-new.tsx (imported as LeadsClient). leads-client.tsx is NOT used. Route: extended app/api/tenant/leads/route.ts GET to validate query params via existing validateQuery + zod (extended leadQuerySchema in lib/api/schemas.ts). New/validated params: source (string), assigned_to (uuid), lifecycle_stage (string), tags (comma-separated string; every listed tag must be present via Drizzle arrayContains -> Postgres @>), score_min / score_max (z.coerce.number int 0..1000), plus lead_status, sort_by, sort_order now validated. All filters composed as additional Drizzle where-clauses AND'd into the existing filters array, preserving tenant scoping (eq(leads.tenantId,...) + deletedAt) and the leads.view_all record-visibility restriction. UI: added an 'Filters' toggle button (with active-count badge) in the toolbar of leads-client-new.tsx and a collapsible filter panel with: Source <select>, Assigned To <select>, Lifecycle Stage <select>, Tags text input (comma separated), and numeric Score min/max inputs, plus a Clear filters button. Filter state is wired into load()'s URLSearchParams and added to the load useCallback + effect deps so applying/clearing any filter refetches from offset 0; existing search (debounced q), status KPI filter, sort, and prev/next pagination preserved. Option sources: Source options merged from real distinct data (page.tsx already passes `sources` = distinct lead_source distribution) with the known SOURCE_LABELS enum as fallback; Assigned To uses real teamMembers already passed to the client; Lifecycle Stage uses the known LIFECYCLE_STAGES enum (no per-tenant distinct query exists for it). Cleanup: the client previously destructured a never-passed `_sources` prop; switched to the real `sources` prop and tightened its type from Record<string,unknown>[] to { lead_source: string|null; count?: unknown }[] (also removed an eslint-disable any). Tests: no leads-route HTTP test harness exists (tests/unit has lead-convert/lead-scoring/lead-warming only), so per instructions did not invent one; instead extended the existing tests/unit/schemas.test.ts with 2 cases covering leadQuerySchema coercion/validation of the new filter params. Verification: npm run typecheck 0 errors; npm run lint 0 errors / 153 warnings (baseline unchanged, touched files 0 warnings); npm run test:unit 5389 pass (baseline 5387 + 2 new). No package-lock changes.
